theme: Phase I and II xenobiotic and drug metabolism
story: The centre is oxidative phase I metabolism of foreign and endogenous compounds: cytochrome P450 reactions (oxidative demethylation, CYP1A2 N-hydroxylation and N-dealkylation of aromatic amines) and flavin monooxygenase oxidation of nucleophiles, with FMO3 deficiency causing trimethylaminuria as the disease example. Phase II conjugations (cytosolic sulfonation, acetylation) complete the detoxification. Steroid, alkaloid, polyketide and nitrogen-compound handling are the substrate classes, so the cluster as a whole describes how the liver chemically modifies lipophilic molecules so they can be excreted.

theme: Cardiac calcium cycling controlling contraction and relaxation
story: The core is excitation-contraction coupling in cardiomyocytes: release of sequestered calcium from the sarcoplasmic reticulum to trigger contraction, and SERCA-mediated reuptake into the SR to allow relaxation. Terms on regulating ATPase-coupled calcium transport and negative regulation of ATP-dependent activity reflect phospholamban-type brakes on SERCA, while membrane potential, heart rate and ion homeostasis terms supply the electrical side. Together they describe how calcium handling sets the strength, timing and relaxation of each heartbeat.

theme: Nutrient and hormonal control of insulin secretion
story: The centre is regulation of insulin secretion by pancreatic beta cells: glucose-stimulated secretion amplified by the incretins GLP-1 and GIP, fatty acids acting through FFAR1/GPR40 and intracellular metabolism, and acetylcholine, and inhibited by adrenaline and noradrenaline; TALK potassium channels tune beta-cell excitability. Insulin processing, insulin catabolism, insulin receptor recycling and insulin-stimulated glucose import cover the hormone's maturation, action and clearance, and glucagon secretion represents the opposing islet hormone. The cluster as a whole describes how the islet matches hormone output to nutrient state.

theme: Early kidney development from intermediate mesoderm to ureter
story: The cluster follows the early kidney lineage: intermediate mesoderm gives rise to the pronephros, then the nephric (mesonephric/Wolffian) duct forms and elongates, and the ureteric bud buds from it to induce the metanephros and form the ureter. Regulation of mesonephros and metanephros development, pattern specification, epithelial tube formation and negative regulation and size control of the kidney provide the regulatory layer. Together these describe how the successive embryonic kidneys and their duct system are laid down and sized.

theme: Mitotic division from entry through cytokinesis
story: This is a full picture of the mitotic cell cycle: kinases (PLK1, Aurora A activated by TPX2, NEK9/6/7, MASTL) drive entry, centrosome maturation and separation, nuclear envelope and lamina breakdown, chromosome condensation, spindle assembly and kinetochore attachment, while cohesion is established, protected at centromeres and then resolved. The spindle assembly checkpoint (MAD2 signalling, Emi1 and direct APC/C inhibition) holds anaphase until the APC/C with Cdc20 and later Cdh1 degrades securin, cyclins A and B, Nek2A and Cdc20 to trigger chromatid separation and mitotic exit. Late events, namely nuclear envelope resealing by ESCRT-III, spindle midzone and contractile ring assembly, septin organization and midbody abscission, plus CENP-A deposition at centromeres, complete the process of producing two daughter cells.

theme: Germinal centre B cell activation and humoral memory
story: The centre is antigen-driven B cell activation in lymphoid follicles: germinal centre formation and B cell differentiation, proliferation and survival, captured both by GO terms and by B-cell-enriched blood transcriptional modules. T follicular helper differentiation and co-stimulation through ICOS and CD27 provide the T cell help that drives these reactions, and negative regulation of proliferation and B cell homeostasis keep them bounded. The output is antibody-mediated humoral immunity and long-lived memory B cells.

theme: Transition and heavy metal homeostasis and detoxification
story: The centre is cellular handling of zinc, copper and manganese: SLC39 importers and SLC30 exporters, copper import and transmembrane transport, and organelle compartmentalization, with metallothioneins and the metal-responsive transcription factor MTF1 buffering excess. Responses to toxic metals (cadmium, mercury, lead, cobalt, selenium) and metal-driven oxidative stress (HMOX1, redox state, hydrogen peroxide metabolism, ferroptosis) form the stress side, while acrodermatitis enteropathica and aceruloplasminemia are the inherited deficiency disorders. The cluster as a whole is about keeping essential metals available while sequestering toxic ones.

theme: APC/C-mediated degradation driving mitotic exit
story: The centre is the anaphase-promoting complex/cyclosome as a ubiquitin ligase: APC/C:Cdc20 destroys securin, cyclin B, cyclin A and Nek2A to release sister chromatids and lower CDK activity, and APC/C:Cdh1 later degrades Cdc20 and other targets in late mitosis and early G1. APC/C phosphorylation and its direct inhibition, together with regulation of ligase activity, are the switches that time these events. The cluster as a whole describes how ordered proteolysis drives exit from mitosis.

theme: RIG-I-like receptor sensing and type I interferon antiviral response
story: Cytosolic viral RNA is sensed by RIG-I and MDA5, signalling through TRAF3 and TRAF6 to IRF7 and NF-kB to induce interferon-alpha and interferon-beta, with OTU deubiquitinases and other negative regulators restraining the pathway. The interferons then induce stimulated genes such as ISG15 (with ISGylation), the OAS system and IP-10, captured by the interferon-alpha hallmark and antiviral signatures. RSV and SARS-CoV terms show viruses evading or modulating this axis, so the cluster as a whole describes the innate antiviral interferon programme from sensing to effector genes.

theme: SWI/SNF BAF chromatin remodeling and nucleosome organization
story: The centre is assembly of the SWI/SNF chromatin remodelers in their different forms (canonical, polybromo, non-canonical, embryonic stem cell and neuronal BAF), together with CHD1/CHD2 remodelers. Nucleosome organization, replication-coupled chromatin assembly, protein-DNA complex disassembly and recruitment of proteins to chromatin describe what these complexes do. RUNX1 cofactors, histone arginine methylation and nucleotide-excision repair regulation are contexts where remodeling controls DNA access, so the cluster is about making chromatin accessible for transcription, replication and repair.

theme: Renin-angiotensin control of blood pressure and fluid volume
story: The centre is the renin-angiotensin system: angiotensinogen is processed to angiotensins, which signal through their receptors to regulate blood volume and systemic arterial pressure. Downstream outputs include renal sodium excretion, urine volume and thirst-driven drinking behaviour, while nervous control of blood pressure adds the neural arm. Bradykinin and neuropeptide catabolism reflect the peptidases such as ACE that both produce angiotensin II and degrade vasodilator peptides, so the cluster describes body fluid and pressure homeostasis.

theme: Innate social, reproductive and exploratory behaviours
story: The cluster gathers organismal behaviours studied mainly in rodents: male and female mating, parental care, aggression, grooming and other intraspecies interactions. Exploration, swimming, psychomotor behaviour and prepulse inhibition (a measure of sensorimotor gating) form the locomotor and sensorimotor side. Amygdala development provides a neural substrate for social and emotional behaviour, so the whole is about the brain-driven behavioural repertoire of an animal.

theme: Biosynthesis of specialized pro-resolving lipid mediators
story: The centre is enzymatic conversion of omega-3 fatty acids (DHA, EPA, DPA n-3 and n-6) into resolvins (D-, E-, aspirin-triggered and 13-series), protectins, maresins and their tissue-regeneration conjugates, plus arachidonate-derived lipoxins and 5- and 15-HETE precursors. Leukotriene B4, lipoxin and eicosanoid catabolism via fatty acid omega-oxidation in the ER provides the inactivation arm, and electrophilic oxo-derivatives add further signalling lipids. The cluster as a whole describes how lipid mediators switch inflammation from initiation to active resolution and tissue repair.

theme: Selective autophagy of organelles
story: The centre is selective autophagy targeting specific organelles: peroxisomes (pexophagy), ER (reticulophagy), mitochondria (receptor-mediated mitophagy) and pieces of the nucleus. Autophagosome assembly, recruitment of proteins to the phagophore assembly site, ATG8 delipidation and control of autophagosome maturation are the shared machinery, and UFMylation marks ER for ER-phagy. Nitrogen-level responses represent the nutrient trigger, so the cluster as a whole is about recycling organelles by autophagy.

theme: Ovarian follicle development, oocyte maturation and ovulation
story: The centre is the ovarian cycle: germ cell migration and proliferation, activation of meiosis and oocyte maturation, follicle growth to the antral stage, ovulation, luteinization, progesterone synthesis and luteolysis. Estrous cycle, gonadotropin feedback and progesterone responses are the endocrine control that sets the rhythm, and positive and negative regulation of cell maturation and female gonad development add regulatory terms. Sertoli cell proliferation is the male somatic counterpart, so the cluster as a whole describes gonadal production of fertilizable gametes and the hormones that time it.

theme: Cholesterol efflux and reverse cholesterol transport
story: The centre is cellular cholesterol efflux to HDL, driven by LXR (NR1H3/NR1H2) induction of efflux transporters and apolipoprotein A-I signalling. Positive and negative regulation of efflux, intracellular lipid transport, cholesterol storage and pinocytosis determine how much sterol a macrophage keeps, and prevention of foam cell formation is the atherosclerosis-relevant outcome. HDL clearance closes the reverse cholesterol transport route to the liver, so the cluster is about whole-body and cellular sterol homeostasis.

theme: RIG-I/MDA5 viral RNA sensing inducing type I interferon
story: The centre is cytosolic detection of viral double-stranded RNA by RIG-I and MDA5. Signalling activates IRF3 to induce type I interferon and activates NF-kB through TRAF6 and FADD/RIP1/caspase-8 routes, with both positive and negative regulators tuning the sensors. The cluster as a whole describes the first innate antiviral alarm in infected cells and how it is restrained to avoid excess inflammation.

theme: Cellular transport of iron, zinc, copper and manganese
story: The centre is membrane transport of essential transition metals: zinc influx and efflux via SLC39 and SLC30, copper import and detoxification, manganese and cobalt transport, and iron handling through the transferrin endocytic cycle, ferroportin (SLC40A1) export, DMT1 (SLC11A2) and ceruloplasmin, plus heme transport. The disease terms (hemochromatosis type 4, iron-overload anemia, aceruloplasminemia, acrodermatitis enteropathica) show what fails when single transporters are defective. The cluster as a whole describes how cells and tissues acquire, distribute and export metal nutrients.

theme: Glycerol backbone and triglyceride synthesis
story: The centre is the glycerolipid pathway: glycerol and glycerol-3-phosphate are acylated to phosphatidic acid, then to diacylglycerol and triacylglycerol, with monoacylglycerol synthesis and acyl-chain remodeling. Aquaglyceroporin transport of glycerol from adipocytes to the liver (with urea transport by the same channel family) connects lipolysis to hepatic reuse. Alditol and fructose metabolism are related three- and six-carbon routes feeding the same triose pool, so the cluster describes how carbon is stored as and recovered from fat.

theme: Nucleotide-sugar and PAPS supply for glycosaminoglycan sulfation
story: The centre is production and transport of the activated donors needed to build sulfated proteoglycans: UDP-glucuronate formation, nucleotide-sugar transporters including SLC35D1, and PAPS synthesis (PAPSS2) and transport, with the sulfate transporter SLC26A2. The disease terms (SEMD-PA, Schneckenbecken dysplasia, SLC26A2 chondrodysplasias) show that failures here cause skeletal dysplasias because cartilage matrix is undersulfated. Hyaluronan degradation and arylsulfatase activation (cysteine oxidation to formylglycine) cover glycosaminoglycan turnover, so the cluster is about making and remodeling cartilage matrix sugars.

theme: Non-vesicular lipid transfer at ER membrane contact sites
story: The centre is lipid transfer proteins moving lipids between membranes without vesicles: phosphatidylinositol and phosphatidylcholine exchange between ER and Golgi, glycolipid, glycosphingolipid and ceramide-1-phosphate transport, and intermembrane phospholipid transfer. ER-plasma membrane tethering, ER tubular network organization, ER positioning and membrane bending provide the contact-site architecture where this happens, and PI synthesis supplies the transferred lipid. The cluster as a whole describes how the ER distributes lipids to other organelles.

theme: Glycolysis, gluconeogenesis and fructose metabolism
story: The centre is glycolysis through glucose-6-phosphate, fructose-6-phosphate and fructose-1,6-bisphosphate, and its reversal in gluconeogenesis. Fructose catabolism and biosynthesis join at these intermediates, with essential fructosuria and hereditary fructose intolerance as the disorders, while GLUT1 deficiency and hexokinase deficiency mark the glucose entry steps. Alanine metabolism supplies gluconeogenic carbon, so the cluster is about central hexose carbon flux.

theme: Obsolete GO terms for vesicle tethering to Golgi
story: All five members are retired GO terms describing tethering and targeting of transport vesicles, specifically to, from and within the Golgi and from rough ER to cis-Golgi. Biologically they describe the docking step of early secretory traffic before SNARE fusion. The cluster is coherent in meaning but consists only of obsolete annotations rather than active pathways.

theme: IL-17/Th17 and IL-1 family cytokine signalling
story: The centre is the Th17 axis: IL-23 production, Th17 lineage commitment, IL-17 production and IL-17A signalling, with CXCL1 induction as the neutrophil-recruiting output. IL-1 family members IL-33, IL-36 and the antagonist IL-38 act as epithelial alarm signals in the same barrier-inflammation setting, and IL-10 production and negative regulation of IL-17 provide restraint. The cluster as a whole describes cytokine-driven inflammation at barrier tissues.

theme: Glutamate, glutamine and aspartate in nitrogen handling
story: The centre is glutamate and glutamine metabolism as the main carriers of amino nitrogen, linked to aspartate and asparagine metabolism by transamination. Arginine catabolism, citrulline metabolism, ammonium responses and ammonium homeostasis connect these amino acids to urea-cycle disposal of nitrogen. The cluster as a whole describes how cells assimilate, shuttle and detoxify nitrogen.

theme: microRNA biogenesis, turnover and translational repression
story: The centre is control of microRNA abundance: regulation of primary and precursor miRNA processing and miRNA decay, including target-directed miRNA degradation. Translational regulation of specific mRNAs (CDH1, CDH11, PD-L1, NPAS4) by microRNAs shows the functional output. The cluster as a whole describes how miRNA levels are set and used to silence target transcripts.

theme: Glycolysis, gluconeogenesis, fructose and glycerol metabolism
story: The centre is the glycolytic/gluconeogenic route through fructose-6-phosphate and fructose-1,6-bisphosphate, with fructose-2,6-bisphosphate as the key allosteric switch between the two directions. Fructose catabolism and biosynthesis (with essential fructosuria and hereditary fructose intolerance) and glycerol, glycerol-3-phosphate and alditol metabolism feed into the same triose and hexose phosphates, while hexokinase deficiency marks the entry step. The cluster as a whole describes central carbohydrate flux and its reciprocal regulation.

theme: Actin polymerization dynamics driving protrusion and motility
story: The centre is control of actin filament assembly: polymerization and depolymerization, Arp2/3 nucleation, formins activated by Rho GTPases, barbed-end capping, severing, crosslinking and parallel bundling. These dynamics build lamellipodia, ruffles, pseudopodia and podosomes and drive substrate-dependent migration, contraction-based motility and macropinocytosis or pinocytosis. Caspase cleavage of cytoskeletal proteins and mast cell chemotaxis are specific contexts, so the cluster describes how the actin cytoskeleton powers cell movement and membrane protrusion.

theme: Antimicrobial peptides and mucosal innate defense
story: The centre is production and action of antimicrobial peptides, chiefly alpha- and beta-defensins, which kill bacteria and fungi by disrupting membranes, cytolysis and agglutination, with peptidoglycan metabolism reflecting cell-wall-targeting enzymes. Nutritional immunity (metal sequestration, competition with heme and siderophore-based iron uptake, as in Mtb) is the second weapon. Regulation of peptide production, neutrophil cytotoxicity and symbiont interaction positions the whole as mucosal innate defense against microbes.

theme: Transcriptional control of adipogenesis and lipid-energy metabolism
story: The centre is the nuclear receptor and transcriptional network that makes and runs fat cells: PPARG with MLL3/4, PPARA, SREBP, LXR (NR1H2/3) and EBF2 control white, brown and beige adipocyte differentiation, lipogenesis, triglyceride synthesis and lipolysis. PGC-1alpha activation and mitochondrial biogenesis link to thermogenesis and gluconeogenesis, and the circadian clock (BMAL1, CLOCK, ROR, REV-ERB) times these programmes. Leptin, caloric restriction and fatty acid and fructose responses show adipose tissue as an endocrine organ tuning whole-body energy balance.

theme: Nephron formation from metanephric mesenchyme
story: The centre is nephrogenesis: metanephric mesenchyme cells, maintained as a progenitor pool, undergo mesenchymal-to-epithelial transition to form renal vesicles, which become tubules patterned along a proximal-distal axis and differentiate into nephron epithelium. The ureteric bud and nephric duct, from intermediate mesoderm through the pronephros, provide the inducing epithelium. The cluster as a whole describes how the kidney builds its nephrons.

theme: Metanephric mesenchyme to nephron epithelium transition
story: The centre is nephron induction in the metanephric kidney: progenitor maintenance, differentiation of metanephric mesenchyme cells and their mesenchymal-to-epithelial transition into tubule epithelium. Intermediate mesoderm, pronephros development and pattern specification set the developmental context. The cluster describes how the kidney converts mesenchyme into nephron tubules.

theme: ER protein targeting, folding, quality control and export
story: The centre is the life of secretory proteins in the ER: SRP-dependent cotranslational targeting, post-translational and tail-anchored insertion, stop-transfer membrane anchoring, folding, and ER quality control including demannosylation, ERAD and retrotranslocation to the cytosol. Exit is handled by COPII cargo concentration and coat formation, ER exit sites and vesicle targeting and fusion at the Golgi, while ER retention and UPR regulation keep the system balanced. The cluster as a whole describes how the ER imports, folds, checks and dispatches membrane and secreted proteins.

theme: E2F-driven G1/S transition and DNA replication initiation
story: The centre is E2F transcription driving the G1/S programme: E2F target gene sets, E2F6 repression and blood transcriptional cell-cycle modules mark proliferating cells. These genes carry out replication origin licensing and firing, DNA unwinding and mitotic-cycle DNA replication, with positive and negative regulation of replication initiation. G1/S and G2/M transition terms place them in the cycle, so the cluster describes the proliferative signature of cells committing to S phase.

theme: Transsulfuration, sulfur amino acids and vitamin B6
story: The centre is transsulfuration, which converts homocysteine to cysteine through PLP-dependent enzymes that also generate hydrogen sulfide, followed by cysteine catabolism and oxidation of sulfide to sulfate. Vitamin B6 activation to pyridoxal phosphate and serine catabolism supply the cofactor and the co-substrate, while molybdenum cofactor synthesis serves sulfite oxidase at the end of sulfur oxidation. The cluster as a whole is about sulfur amino acid disposal and its cofactor dependence.

theme: Golgi nucleotide-sugar supply: GDP-fucose and CMP-sialic acid
story: The centre is provision of donor sugars for Golgi glycosylation: GDP-fucose biosynthesis and metabolism, and transport of GDP-fucose (SLC35C1) and CMP-sialic acid (SLC35A1) into the Golgi. Their defects cause congenital disorders of glycosylation types 2C and 2F. The cluster describes how fucosylation and sialylation depend on getting activated sugars to the glycosyltransferases.

theme: Tooth and bone mineralization
story: The centre is biomineralization of hard tissues: enamel, dentin and cementum formation, odontoblast differentiation and tooth eruption, alongside positive and negative regulation of bone mineralization. Post-translational phosphorylation of secreted proteins reflects kinases that phosphorylate matrix proteins controlling crystal growth, and SLC24A4 amelogenesis imperfecta shows a mineral-ion transport defect. Chondrocyte development adds the cartilage template, so the cluster describes how teeth and bone become mineralized.

theme: Sprouting angiogenesis via VEGF and FGF signalling
story: The centre is sprouting angiogenesis: endothelial cell proliferation, chemotaxis and migration form and branch new vessels, driven by VEGF receptor signalling. FGF receptor signalling, FGF production and chemotaxis to FGF provide a second growth factor input, with positive and negative regulators setting the balance. The cluster as a whole describes how new blood vessels grow.

theme: Monoamine neurotransmitter synthesis, release and reuptake
story: The centre is catecholamine and serotonin neurotransmission: dopamine and catecholamine biosynthesis, vesicular loading, the norepinephrine release cycle, and reuptake by SLC6 transporters (DAT for dopamine, NET for norepinephrine, and serotonin uptake). The disease terms (DAT defects causing infantile parkinsonism-dystonia, NET defects causing orthostatic intolerance) show what clearance failure does. Regulation of secretion, uptake and spontaneous transmission, plus obsolete transport terms, round out a cluster describing the monoaminergic synapse.

theme: Host-pathogen interface: antimicrobial defence and bacterial evasion
story: The host side is the antimicrobial arsenal of neutrophils and mucosa: degranulation, defensins and other antimicrobial peptides, metal sequestration, phagosome acidification and phagolysosome fusion, and mucus and microbiota control. The pathogen side, largely Mycobacterium tuberculosis, counters with blocking phagosome acidification and lysosome fusion, suppressing apoptosis, autophagy and nitric oxide, inhibiting membrane repair, manipulating host metabolism and attaching to or entering epithelial cells. The cluster as a whole describes the contest between host killing mechanisms and bacterial strategies to survive inside phagocytes.

theme: Axon guidance by netrin, Slit-Robo, semaphorin and ephrin cues
story: The centre is axon guidance: netrin/DCC attraction and repulsion, Slit-Robo repulsion at the midline, semaphorin-plexin repulsion via CRMPs and PAK, and ephrin-Eph contact repulsion. These cues converge on Rho-family GTPases (RAC1, RAC3, CDC42, RHOA) to collapse or extend the growth cone, steering commissural axons, retinal ganglion cell axons in the optic nerve and fasciculating bundles. Dendrite branching and negative chemotaxis extend the same machinery, so the cluster describes how neurons wire their projections.

theme: Circadian clock feedback loop and metabolic outputs
story: The centre is the molecular clock: BMAL1:CLOCK/NPAS2 activate core clock genes, CRY:PER kinase complexes are phosphorylated, enter the nucleus and repress their own activators and are then degraded, and ROR and REV-ERB (with heme as REV-ERB ligand) control BMAL1 expression. Photoperiod entrainment and locomotor rhythm are the physiological input and output. PGC-1alpha, PPARA, mitochondrial biogenesis and fatty acid responses show how the clock times metabolism, with NPAS4 as an activity-dependent relative.

theme: Germinal centre B cell and Tfh help signature
story: The centre is B cell identity and activation, captured mostly by blood transcriptional modules enriched in B cells, naive and memory B cells and memory B cell surface markers. Germinal centre B cell differentiation, B cell proliferation, Tfh differentiation and ICOS co-stimulation describe the T-dependent germinal centre reaction that generates memory. The cluster as a whole is about antigen-experienced B cell responses that produce adaptive immune memory.

theme: Basement membrane and ECM-integrin adhesion
story: The centre is building the basement membrane and the cell-matrix adhesions that anchor to it: laminin interactions, collagen trimerization, anchoring fibrils, fibronectin matrix, proteoglycans and elastic-fibre molecules. Cells grip this matrix through integrins, hemidesmosomes, the dystrophin-glycoprotein complex and collagen-activated receptor tyrosine kinases. Acetylcholine receptor clustering at the neuromuscular junction is a specialised basement-membrane-dependent output, so the cluster describes tissue anchoring to the extracellular matrix.

theme: Platelet activation and degranulation
story: The centre is platelet activation by agonist receptors: ADP via P2Y1 and P2Y12, thrombin via PARs and thromboxane via the TP receptor, with LDL sensitizing and prostacyclin opposing activation. Activation drives cytoskeletal remodelling and integrin-based adhesion (talin, ILK, Rho regulation) and SNARE-mediated granule secretion, captured by degranulation terms and platelet blood transcriptional modules. The cluster as a whole describes how platelets switch on to form a haemostatic plug.

theme: Mitotic spindle, sister chromatid cohesion and checkpoint
story: The centre is chromosome segregation in mitosis: establishment, centromeric protection and resolution of sister chromatid cohesion, followed by chromatid separation. PLK1, Aurora A (with PHLDA1 and FBXL7 regulation) and NEK kinases control centrosome separation and spindle formation, and the MAD2-based spindle assembly checkpoint holds anaphase until all kinetochores are attached. The cluster as a whole describes how the mitotic spindle and cohesion ensure accurate chromosome segregation.

theme: Inflammasome-driven pyroptosis and IL-18
story: The centre is inflammasome activation: AIM2 senses cytosolic DNA and IPAF (NLRC4) senses bacterial components, assembling caspase-1 platforms. These trigger gasdermin-mediated pyroptotic cell death and IL-18 maturation and signalling. Bacterial antagonism of host defence and defective pyroptosis show how pathogens and mutations disable this, so the cluster describes inflammatory cell death as a defence against intracellular bacteria.

theme: Meiotic chromosome pairing, recombination and segregation
story: The centre is meiotic prophase I: programmed DNA double-strand breaks, homolog synapsis and synaptonemal complex assembly, and chiasma formation that physically link homologs. Meiotic cohesion establishment and centromeric protection, metaphase alignment, movement to the poles and the metaphase-anaphase transition carry out reductional segregation, including in female meiosis. Meiotic checkpoints and negative regulation of meiotic progression ensure errors halt division, so the cluster describes faithful halving of the chromosome set.

theme: Post-Golgi and endosomal membrane trafficking
story: The centre is traffic between the trans-Golgi network, endosomes and lysosomes: Golgi-associated vesicle biogenesis, Golgi-to-endosome and Golgi-to-lysosome transport, protein targeting to lysosomes and lysosome vesicle biogenesis. Retrograde transport from early and late endosomes back to the Golgi, plasma membrane-to-endosome uptake and endosomal fusion complete the loop, with constitutive secretion as the outbound route. Rab signalling and TBC Rab-GAPs regulate the whole network, which sorts proteins between secretion, recycling and degradation.

theme: DNA double-strand break sensing and repair pathway choice
story: The centre is the response to DNA double-strand breaks: break sensing and ATM-mediated phosphorylation of repair and signalling proteins at the break. Repair proceeds either by classical or alternative non-homologous end joining or by homologous recombination, with positive and negative regulators determining the choice. BRCA1, BARD1 and BRCA2 defects (including impaired BRCA2 nuclear import and SEM1 binding) show how loss of HR leads to genome instability and cancer predisposition.
